title: NVIDIA Invests $3.5 Billion in MediaTek, Sending the Latter’s Stock Price Soaring to Its Daily Limit

questions.question: Will MediaTek capture approximately 15% of the custom AI-chip market in calendar 2027?
questions.why_it_matters: A substantial share for MediaTek would indicate that a new competitor is gaining meaningful scale in custom AI chips, potentially strengthening an alternative to NVIDIA GPUs and changing NVIDIA’s competitive position. The article cites MediaTek’s target against an $80 billion market, but this is an outlook, not a result.
questions.why_not_already_covered: The existing question about a production deployment of a non-NVIDIA custom XPU using NVLink Fusion (v107) tracks a specific deployment milestone. MediaTek’s market share could change independently of whether such a deployment is publicly confirmed, and the article does not say that a MediaTek design is already deployed in an NVIDIA-connected rack. Existing NVIDIA revenue and market-share questions do not measure MediaTek’s share of the custom AI-chip segment.
questions.how_and_when_to_check: Check after calendar 2027, using public MediaTek disclosures and credible industry estimates of custom AI-chip market size and supplier shares, with a consistent market definition. December 31, 2027 is an analyst check date, not a deadline stated in the article; the article does not specify when or how the share will be measured.

article:
NVIDIA ( NVDA ) has invested $3.5 billion in MediaTek, marking its largest direct investment outside the United States. The move not only propelled MediaTek’s stock price to its daily trading limit but also provided significant validation for MediaTek’s strategic transformation in AI chips. Through technical collaboration, the two companies are deepening custom chip design and data center interconnect capabilities, with MediaTek expecting this business to continue growing and capture a substantial market share. According to the agreement announced on Monday, NVIDIA will purchase convertible bonds that can be exchanged for MediaTek shares, representing NVIDIA’s largest direct investment outside the U.S. to date.
MediaTek was historically known for its fierce competition with Qualcomm ( QCOM ) in the mobile phone chip market, with both companies vying for orders from handset brands such as OPPO. In recent years, however, the company has gradually shifted its business focus toward custom chip design, competing with firms like Broadcom ( AVGO ) and steadily gaining the trust of major technology companies as a partner for their in-house AI chip development. Francis Tan, Chief Strategist at Indosuez Wealth Management in Singapore, stated that this investment represents a significant endorsement of MediaTek’s strategic direction, marking its transformation from a company known primarily for smartphone chips into a broader AI semiconductor player.
Earlier this year, MediaTek already entered into a partnership with Google ( GOOGL ), and some analysts have speculated that SpaceX ( SPCX ) could become its next AI client. This series of positive developments has driven MediaTek’s market capitalization to roughly triple in recent months.
As part of the transaction, MediaTek will allow customers to use NVIDIA’s NVLink Fusion technology to design their own AI chips and connect directly to NVIDIA’s large-scale computing systems. The technology provides off-the-shelf connectors and dedicated memory, enabling custom AI chips to interface with NVIDIA’s data center systems, helping customers save time and engineering costs while allowing them to focus on their own chip designs without having to build interconnects to NVIDIA systems from scratch. In addition, the two companies will continue to collaborate on PC chips and AI automotive technologies. In June of this year, they jointly launched the RTX Spark PC chip, bringing AI capabilities directly to laptops and desktops.
MediaTek’s AI chip business is expected to accelerate further following its collaboration with NVIDIA. Previously, MediaTek estimated that its custom AI chip business would generate $2 billion in revenue this year and plans to capture approximately 15% of the $80 billion market in this segment by 2027.
